messages:
nina: Hey all — first week here. Trying to mirror prod Redis TLS locally. docker-compose says redis is up but my app throws ECONNREFUSED when using rediss:// in REDIS_URL. I'm on mac, using Docker Desktop. Any tips?

chris: Welcome! Can you paste your docker-compose snippet and the REDIS_URL you set?

nina: Minimal compose: ```
version: '3.8'
services:
  redis:
    image: redis:7
    command: ["redis-server", "--tls-port", "6379", "--port", "0", "--tls-cert-file", "/certs/redis.crt", "--tls-key-file", "/certs/redis.key", "--tls-ca-cert-file", "/certs/ca.crt"]
    volumes:
      - ./certs:/certs:ro
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
  web:
    build: .
    environment:
      REDIS_URL: rediss://:p@localhost:6379
    depends_on:
      - redis
```

leo: A couple of things: 1) Inside the web container, localhost points to the container itself, not the redis service. Use the service DNS name (e.g., redis) in REDIS_URL when the app runs in a container. 2) You're starting redis with TLS only (you set --port 0), which is fine if the client uses TLS and has the CA cert.

chris: Also verify your redis binary supports TLS. redis:7 usually does, but some images or builds don't. From your host try: `redis-cli -h localhost -p 6379 --tls --cacert ./certs/ca.crt -a p` to test host connectivity. From the web container try installing redis-cli and run: `redis-cli -h redis -p 6379 --tls --cacert /certs/ca.crt -a p`. If that works, the server is fine.

nina: Tried the redis-cli from inside web container without --tls and got a protocol error. With --tls and pointing to /certs it connected. My Node app still errored because I had REDIS_URL=rediss://:p@localhost:6379 inside the container. Changed to rediss://:p@redis:6379 and mounted certs into web so the process can verify the CA. Now it connects.

leo: For local convenience you can also: a) run redis without TLS locally (remove TLS flags) and use plain redis:// for dev, b) run a small stunnel sidecar that terminates TLS so the app can use plain redis://, or c) keep TLS but ensure certs are mounted into the app container and the client is configured to trust them.

chris: One more gotcha: publishing the port (6379:6379) exposes the TLS port to your Mac. If you want to connect from host with TLS, you must use --tls in redis-cli and provide the CA. If you publish both TLS and non-TLS ports, pick different host ports to avoid collisions.

nina: Sweet — switching host in REDIS_URL to "redis" and adding cert mounts fixed it. Thanks folks! :pray:
